tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with 'Diagnose...' and 'Use this skill when a training job is denied access...' which is imperative and lists many explicit trigger contexts (specific errors, symptoms, and registry conditions) covering both training and registry domains. It focuses on user-facing symptoms (access denied, InsufficientCapacityError, no metrics, rejected packages) rather than internal implementation, and explicitly excludes an adjacent scope (evaluation jobs). It is a dense paragraph but stays within a reasonable length for the breadth of triggers it must cover.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a training job is denied access to S3, a KMS key or iam:PassRole, fails with InsufficientCapacityError, ResourceLimitExceeded or out of memory, goes to Failed with no logs...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body stays domain-specific throughout — check-id tables, router mapping, step procedures — with no generic explanations of SageMaker basics or AWS concepts the agent would already know.
tests.evidence: Grounded in [checks-sagemaker-training.md] ... the LLM-SM-TRAIN-* sub-family for training / customization and the LLM-SM-REG-* sub-family for model registry / lineage

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed catalogs (full check descriptions, API quirks, known causes) are kept in references/ files and only a compact what-it-catches index table and router table appear in the body, both reasonably sized summary tables rather than full reference dumps.
tests.evidence: The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference; the table below is a what-it-catches index.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown links in the body (checks-sagemaker-training.md, collection-reference.md, api-quirks.md, known-causes.md, metrics-and-logs.md).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with a specific triggering condition describing when to load it.
tests.evidence: Load [known-causes.md](references/known-causes.md) whenever the user names an error or symptom (training §1–§7, Model Registry §8–§14); match it to a section

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (capacity-vs-quota classification, severity assignment, guardrails) are given exact prescriptive steps, while review scoping and report assembly leave room for judgment with rationale explained.
tests.evidence: The capacity-vs-quota split is opposite remediations: read both the FailureReason and the quota value

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present competing tools as equal options; it prescribes specific read-only APIs per symptom in the router table as the default path.
tests.evidence: The Router table maps each symptom directly to a specific API call and reference, with no alternative tools offered as equals.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable classification and review procedure (Review Procedure checklist, router by symptom) rather than declaring a single fixed task instance.
tests.evidence: Classify before prescribing anything. Run the steps in order and track progress against this checklist.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' and 'Error Handling' section documenting non-obvious API quirks and misleading signals specific to this domain.
tests.evidence: "The job is InProgress with Pending, so it is failing." A job waiting on GPU capacity is control-plane-healthy, not Failed.
